kill_argument: Neither decisive label says anything about AB 1228. H1's 'not supported' is set by one data break in one placebo state: the four largest of the 60 decision-set wage t-values (4.54, 4.32, 3.45, 3.31) are all Georgia's, at 2016Q1-2016Q4, whose trend windows straddle a 15-log-point drop in Georgia's 722513 weekly wage between 2014 and 2015, the largest break in the panel. Georgia sets the cutoff at 3.45 against t_nu = 1.76. Without Georgia, the pooled t of 2.66 and both yearly t-values reject. So the 'no first stage' reading, the dropped elasticities and 'H2 uninformative about the wage floor' all rest on a Georgia artifact. H2's 'inconclusive' was fixed before any post-period data were read: level-mde gives it probability 0.95 at tau = 0 and 0.83 at -0.035, and gives 'smaller than 2%' probability 0. The test cannot separate the published readings, as the contribution claims. What held: select ran once on the truncated panel; level-mde preceded every post run; every label follows the coded rule; the jobs, dollar and percent conversions recompute; and the max SE is justified by California's scaled-SE level check.

findings.text: H1's verdict, and everything that follows from it, is set by Georgia alone. The H1 critical values come from the decision-set L quantile (crit_h1_hi95 = 3.449 and crit_h1_hi975 = 4.320, both from_L = 1; t_nu = 1.758 and 2.139). In runs/level-mde/tests.csv the top four of the 60 L wage t-values are Georgia at 2016Q1-2016Q4 (4.54, 4.32, 3.45, 3.31). The other nine L states have max 1.13, and Georgia itself gives -0.35 and 0.11 at 2017Q1-Q2. In data/derived/state_panel_pre.csv Georgia's 722513 average weekly wage is 287-304 in 2014 (above California's) and 255-276 in 2015. Its year-over-year log change, measured against the cross-state median, is -0.150 to -0.170 in 2015Q1-Q4. That is the largest break in the panel (the next is FL 2018Q4 at -0.078), and the employment series shows no break. That pattern fits a reporting or classification change (not verified). The DDT trend over B'-8..B' straddles the break exactly at the pseudo-dates 2016Q1-2016Q4 and not after it. Without Georgia's six values, the L q95 and q975 are 0.75 and 0.76, so c_hi = t_nu. Then the pooled H1 (t 2.66), year 1 (2.04) and year 2 (2.99) all reject, and the 95% interval lower end is about +0.018. My computation from the run outputs; report-only, not a proposed verdict. The same quantile sets MDE_h1 = 0.148, the anticipation wage interval's lower end (c_hi975 = 4.32), the 'not computed' elasticities and 'H2 uninformative about the wage floor'. runs/NOTES.md item 5 notes the surprise but does not trace it, and no claim mentions it. The verdict follows the pre-specified rule and should stand, but as worded r-v-h1, r-v-h2-note and r-h1-wage-h1-c-hi95 invite the reading 'no detectable first stage', which the run outputs do not support.
findings.evidence: runs/level-mde/metrics.json crit_h1_*, Lq_h1_*, tnu_h1_*, mde_h1; runs/level-mde/tests.csv rows stat=h1, in_L=1; data/derived/state_panel_pre.csv aww_722513 for GA 2014Q1-2015Q4; runs/h1-wage/metrics.json h1_t, h1_y1_t, h1_y2_t, h1_p_upper_tnu 0.009; runs/anticip/metrics.json; claims r-v-h1, r-v-h2-note, r-h1-wage-h1-c-hi95, r-owe-*. Remedy (cheapest; verdict unchanged): add text claims, backed by level-mde, saying that the H1 critical values come from Georgia's four 2016 pseudo-date tests and that the remaining L values never exceed t_nu. Qualify r-v-h1 and r-v-h2-note to 'not supported at the pre-specified L-calibrated critical value'. Put h1_p_upper_tnu next to it. The paper must not say the wage floor had no detectable effect on weekly earnings. A report-only check of Georgia's 2014-2015 722513 wage series against the BLS county files or the QCEW notes would show whether it is an artifact. Any new metric needs a code review round before it runs.

findings.text: The H2 label was effectively decided before any post-period data were read, and the contribution statement cannot survive it. level-mde gives prob(inconclusive) = 0.95 at tau = 0 and 0.829 at tau = -0.035, and prob('smaller than 2%') = 0 under both. h90_h2 = 0.054 > b = 0.02 and MDE_h2 = 0.092, 2.6 times the CEM estimate the bound is meant to test; with the real SE, h2-emp gives 0.107 and 0.063. California's own six H2 placebo t-values have RMS k = 0.37: the max SE is about 2.7 times the spread of California's pseudo-ATTs, so the width comes from the conservative SE, not from noise observed for California. Both published readings (CEM about -3.5%, Dube about 0) lie well inside the 95% CI [-0.106, 0.047]. Yet plan.json contribution still says 'H2 adds an equivalence test against a 2% bound that separates the two published readings', and the H2 text says a CI inside +/-0.02 excludes CEM's median estimates. That outcome had probability 0. The claims are correct as numbers. The finding is scope: 'inconclusive' is the expected outcome under either reading, and the Writer will draft from a contribution sentence the results contradict.

Remedy: narrow the contribution and H2 framing before the paper stage: the pre-specified test could not reach 'smaller than 2%' at this SE. State the label probabilities (already claimed) and k_h2 next to the headline label. Do not describe the result as evidence against either published estimate.
findings.response: PI: plan contribution now says level-mde showed the equivalence test cannot separate the readings at this precision; the claims and paper put the label probabilities and k_h2 next to the headline (Econometrician).

findings.text: The out-of-fit pre-period evidence the design names for DDT is not in the claims. identifying_assumption (ii) says the seven 2022Q1-2023Q3 event-path gaps are DDT's trend fit points (curvature only) and that 'DDT's out-of-fit pre-period evidence is the 2014-2019 segment of the path'. The claims report only the in-fit segment: RMS 0.006 and 0 bands excluding 0. In runs/event-path/event_path.csv the 2014-2019 detrended employment gap rises steadily from -0.045 (2014Q1) to -0.002 (2019Q4), an OLS slope of 0.0023 per quarter. The wage gap rises from -0.245 to -0.044, 0.0085 per quarter. So the relative trend fitted on 2022Q1-2023Q3 (seven post-COVID quarters, extrapolated up to ten quarters) is not the 2014-2019 trend. At the post window's mean horizon of 6.5 quarters the gap in slopes is about 0.015 log points for employment (three-quarters of b) and about 0.055 for wages (60% of the H1 estimate). The bands are wide (SE 0.07-0.15), so no single quarter 'fails'. But a claim set showing only the in-fit RMS reads as a pre-trend pass that the design itself says it is not.
findings.evidence: runs/event-path/event_path.csv rows quarter 2014Q1-2019Q4, outcomes emp and wage; runs/event-path/metrics.json (no 2014-2019 metric); plan.json design.identifying_assumption (ii), design.method ESTIMATORS DDT (7 trend points for the real B, 9 at pseudo-dates); claims r-event-emp-2022q1-2023q3-rms-gap, r-event-case. Remedy: report the 2014-2019 segment as DDT's out-of-fit evidence, either as a report-only metric (slope or RMS of the 2014-2019 detrended gap) added to event_path.py, which needs a code review before it runs, or in the fig-event caption and a text claim. Add a limitation: the DDT counterfactual extrapolates a seven-quarter post-COVID trend that differs from the 2014-2019 one.

findings.text: S2 (Dube SDID) fails California's own pre-period level check, yet its interval will stand in the abstract next to the primary. California's six S2 pseudo-ATTs are all positive, +0.024 to +0.034 (mean about +0.029, larger than b), with t from 1.55 to 2.12. k_s2_se = 1.86, and California's one-sided upper rejection rate is 4 of 6 (3 of 6 at t_nu) even with the max SE and the SDID floor. S2's 95% interval [-0.047, 0.028] is the narrowest of the three, and its reused-weights wage interval [0.035, 0.116] excludes 0. Both come from the procedure whose pre-period behaviour for California is worst. The label ('inconclusive') is not wrong. The risk is reading S2's narrower interval as support for a near-zero effect, or as an independent confirmation of the first stage in R1.

findings.text: The plc-nonff qualifier does not give the direction. California's employment outside 722513 ran +2.45% above the counterfactual (95% CI [0.003, 0.046]), the same size as |H2|. If the same California-wide deviation reached 722513, the H2 estimate is biased toward zero or positive, not toward a decline. 'Not separable from a California-wide shock' leaves the reader to guess.
findings.evidence: runs/plc-nonff/metrics.json plc_att, plc_lo95, plc_hi95; runs/verdict/metrics.json h2_label_qualified; claims r-plc-nonff-*, r-v-h2-qualified. Remedy: a text claim stating the sign. No numerical adjustment of H2, because none was pre-specified.

findings.text: The fit numbers hide bias. The selected candidate's six pseudo-ATTs are all positive (0.0001 to 0.0154, mean 0.010), so most of the selection RMSE of 0.0112 is a systematic shortfall of the counterfactual, not noise. On wages the same estimator gives California's six pseudo-ATTs all negative (-0.014 to -0.062, mean -0.032, RMS about 0.036, above b). H1 inherits an estimator chosen on employment that fits California's wages poorly before the policy. California's H1 pseudo-ATTs are not claimed; only H2's and S2's are.

Remedy: claim the ca_h1_* pseudo-ATTs, which are already metrics of level-mde, and state the sign pattern next to the RMSE. A mean pseudo-ATT metric would need code review; the text can describe the six claimed values instead.

findings.text: The Ferman-Pinto A + B/pop diagnostic is degenerate for the post-period statistics: h2_fp_a = -0.00043 with h2_fp_se = 0.0, and likewise h1_y1, h3_y1 and h3_y2 (fp_a < 0, fp_se = 0). These are unclaimed, but the California pseudo-date FP diagnostics are claimed (r-ca-*-fpa/fpb/fpse). An SE of 0 must not appear as a standard error. Report the diagnostic only as evidence that the A + B/pop fit fails here, which supports the max-SE choice.

Every level-check rate claim ends 'group t1 (all units, population terciles 1-3 smallest to largest, decision set L, California)': the parenthesis lists every group, not the one the claim is about. The cm_ echo claims end '(rejection rate of California's 5% test, or nu_MC)' whichever metric they carry. For example, r-cm-mc-dd-popw-e-d20-heteroa-ca2-rho05-nu-mc is a df, not a rate.
